question.prompt: A square with side length \(x\) is inscribed in a right triangle with sides of length \(3,\) \(4,\) and \(5\) so that one vertex of the square coincides with the right-angle vertex of the triangle. A square with side length \(y\) is inscribed in another right triangle with sides of length \(3,\) \(4,\) and \(5\) so that one side of the square lies on the hypotenuse of the triangle. What is \(\dfrac{x}{y}?\)

solutions.title: Use similar triangles
solutions.explanation:
The sides of each square create smaller right triangles similar to the original triangle. Name the vertices of each large triangle \(A,B,C\), where \(A\) is the right-angle vertex and
\[
AB=3,\qquad AC=4,\qquad BC=5.
\]

For the first square, name its vertices \(A,D,E,F\) in order, with \(D\) on \(AB\), \(E\) on \(BC\), and \(F\) on \(AC\). Its sides have length \(x\), so
\[
BD=3-x,\qquad FC=4-x.
\]
The triangles \(BDE\) and \(EFC\) are similar: each is right, and their acute angles match because the square's sides are parallel to the triangle's legs. Corresponding side ratios give
\[
\frac{DE}{BD}=\frac{FC}{EF},
\qquad
\frac{x}{3-x}=\frac{4-x}{x}.
\]
Therefore
\[
x^2=(3-x)(4-x)=12-7x+x^2,
\qquad x=\frac{12}{7}.
\]

In the second triangle, name the square's vertices \(D,E,F,G\) in order, with \(D,E\) on \(BC\), \(F\) on \(AC\), and \(G\) on \(AB\). Since \(GF\parallel BC\), triangles \(AGF\) and \(ABC\) are similar. Their hypotenuses are \(GF=y\) and \(BC=5\), so
\[
AG=\frac35y.
\]
Also, \(DG\perp BC\), so the right triangles \(BDG\) and \(BAC\) share angle \(B\) and are similar. Here \(DG=y\) corresponds to \(AC=4\), while \(BG\) corresponds to \(BC=5\). Thus
\[
BG=\frac54y.
\]
Adding the two parts of \(AB\) gives
\[
\frac35y+\frac54y=3,
\qquad
\frac{37}{20}y=3,
\qquad
y=\frac{60}{37}.
\]
Consequently,
\[
\frac{x}{y}=\frac{12}{7}\cdot\frac{37}{60}
=\boxed{\frac{37}{35}},
\]
choice \(\text{(D)}\).
